---
title: "Research Grade observations with only 2 IDs"
format: html
editor: visual
---

Since it's not possible to get the date when observation was upgraded to RG, we crated a subset observations that are RG and have only 2 ID. For these observations the date of the last update corresponds to the date in got RG status.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false

library(tidyverse)

tidy_data_verifiable <- read_csv("../data/tidy_data/tidy_data_verifiable.csv")

research_2ids <- tidy_data_verifiable %>%
        filter(quality_grade  == "research" & n_identifications == 2) %>% 
        mutate(created_at_month = factor(created_at_month, levels = month.abb, ordered = TRUE))

rm(tidy_data_verifiable)

research_2ids <- research_2ids %>% 
        mutate(days_to_RG = as.numeric(as.Date(updated_at) - as.Date(created_at)))


```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
research_2ids <- research_2ids %>%
        arrange(days_to_RG) %>%
        mutate(observation = 1:n())

research_2ids %>% 
        ggplot(aes(x=days_to_RG, y= observation))+
        geom_step() +
        geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) + 
        labs(x = "Number of days to Research Grade", 
             y = "Number of observations") +
        scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number())+
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(research_2ids$days_to_RG), by = 365))+
        theme_minimal()
```

Maximum percentage of observations that were identified in the same day as they were uploaded (day of upload counts as 0) was near 40%. Within 1 year, near 90%.

```{r}
perc <- research_2ids %>% 
        mutate(perc = observation / n()) %>% 
        select(perc, days_to_RG)

perc %>% filter(days_to_RG == 0)  %>% 
        slice_max(order_by = perc, n = 1) 

perc %>% 
        filter(days_to_RG == 365)  %>% 
        slice_max(perc, n = 1) #used max because I want maximum percentage achieved within 1 year

```

For those observations that reached RG with exclusively two IDs, 50% had achieved RG after one day, around 60% after 3 days.

```{r}
perc %>% 
        filter(perc >= 0.5)  %>% 
        slice_min(perc, n = 1) #used min because i want the first day at witch 50% is reached
                  
perc %>% 
        filter(perc >= 0.6)  %>% 
        slice_min(perc, n = 1)

```

#### Easier to look at cumulative proportions:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#Could use ecdf to automatically calculate this but it goes beyond limits of the plot - i think it's because it is a calculated function
# ggplot(research_2ids, aes(x = days_to_RG)) +
#         stat_ecdf(geom = "step") +
#         theme_minimal()

ggplot(perc, aes(x = days_to_RG, y = perc*100)) +
        geom_step(size = 1) +
        labs(x = "Days to Research Grade",
             y = "Cumulative Percentage of Observations") +
        scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(suffix = "%")) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,5000, by = 365)) +
        theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
        theme(axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10 )),
              axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)))
```

**"Zoom in" on 30 days**

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#note: if you wanted to use stat_ecdf() on just the first 30 days you must use coord_cartesian and not scale_x_continuous, because scaling will remove data and therefore change function
ggplot(perc, aes(x = days_to_RG, y = perc*100)) +
        geom_step() +
        labs(x = "Days to Research Grade",
             y = "Cumulative percentage of observations") +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 30)) +
        scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10)) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 4)) +
        theme_classic()
```

### By month

```{r}
#| code-fold: true

research_2ids_test <- research_2ids %>%
  arrange(created_at_month, days_to_RG) %>%  # Sort by month first
  group_by(created_at_month) %>%  # Group by month
  mutate(observation = row_number()) %>%  # Assign observation numbers within each month
  ungroup()

ggplot(research_2ids_test, aes(x = days_to_RG, y = observation, 
                          color = as.factor(created_at_month), 
                          group = created_at_month)) +
  geom_line() +
  #geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "Number of days to Research Grade", 
       y = "Number of observations", 
       color = "Month of upload") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(research_2ids$days_to_RG), by = 365)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### Cumulative proportion of observations:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
ggplot(research_2ids_test, aes(x = days_to_RG, color = created_at_month)) +
        stat_ecdf(geom = "step") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**"Zoom-in" on 30 days:**

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
ggplot(research_2ids_test, aes(x = days_to_RG, color = created_at_month)) +
        stat_ecdf(geom = "step") +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0,30)) +
        theme_minimal()

```

September, October are the ones for which percentage is smaller on day 0 so it takes longer to reach RG. November also has small %. These are also the ones for which there are a lot of observations (see plot below) so it's likely that they get lost in the influx. However, this logic doesn't match for other months - July has the smallest number of observations but also has small percentage - same(ish) as November. In general second half of the year (July to December) does worse.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
percentage_day0 <- research_2ids %>%
          group_by(created_at_month) %>%
          summarise(
            total_obs = n(),
            rg_day0 = sum(days_to_RG == 0),
            percentage_day0 = (rg_day0 / total_obs) *100) %>% 
          select(created_at_month, percentage_day0, total_obs)

knitr::kable(percentage_day0)

```
